without_experience.text: The far-end grasps have not produced reliable support. I’m now testing a slow side-step sequence with the previously working rail grasp, so the robot follows the hands through the full curve. SONIC remains active, with additional joint tracking for the planned foot placements.

Object-pose feedback has improved the stable result to 0.234 m mean ADD, 0.331 m position error, and 17.74° orientation error. It maintains contact and reaches farther along the curve than the frozen submission, but still stops short of upright. The walking variants have been unstable; I’m testing ankle balance feedback and nearby grasp-feedback settings before selecting the final checkpoint.

with_experience.text: The peer reports suggest that bounded pose feedback and feeding the revised arm motion to SONIC can help preserve contact. The shelf also needs more robot travel than the original retarget provides. I’m building a stepping reference that follows the grasp through the rotation, with bounded body-orientation feedback to correct drift.

The stepping trials move the robot farther along the shelf, but the front-end grasp still loses control. I’m testing grasps closer to the shelf’s centre, which should reduce the turning torque and hand height, plus a variant that measures the settled hand-to-shelf transforms before lifting.

A 40% blend of the planned leg motion with SONIC produced a much better result: the shelf reached near the upright endpoint, with contact at every recorded sample. Mean errors were 0.151 m ADD, 0.140 m position, and 14.7° orientation. I’ve preserved it and am checking nearby gains for lower error and better stability.

Bounded object-pose feedback reduced the mean errors to 0.0777 m ADD, 0.0673 m position, and 8.89° orientation, with continuous recorded contact. The shelf reaches upright, but endpoint overshoot remains. I’m finishing an endpoint-settling test, then I’ll freeze and replay the best result.

without_experience.text: I’ll preserve the validated checkpoint—2.92 mm ADD, 2.15 mm position error, and 1.07° orientation error—then use the additional time to reduce the remaining trajectory and endpoint errors. I’ll update the analysis with the final measurements and limitations.

A different right-thumb posture removes the initial thumb/hip overlap and reduces maximum self-penetration from 21.4 mm to about 3.6 mm. With that change, a validated candidate also improves ADD to 2.49 mm. I’m refining this cleaner initialization and checking its tilt amplitude and endpoint.

The search is stopped. I’m preserving the fully validated submission and checking that its files match the recorded execution. Final metrics are 2.405 mm ADD, 1.892 mm position error, and 0.730° orientation error; the analysis includes the remaining tilt undershoot and self-contact.

with_experience.text: The peer reports reinforce two useful lessons: preserve SONIC’s balance behavior when adding corrections, and check whether residual endpoint error comes from scene contact constraints. Here, the remaining error includes gravity settling and the target’s slight final roll. I’ll first refine the existing foot motion and check whether opening the unused Dex3 fingers removes the recorded self-contact.

Moving the right arm slightly outward reduced maximum self-penetration from 21.4 mm to about 3.8 mm while keeping path error near 3 mm. I’m refining that posture and testing small object-orientation feedback through the right hip joints to reduce unwanted yaw during contact.

A small yaw-rate damping term improved ADD and orientation error over the refined reference alone. I’m checking that combination and a thumb-clearance variant. The validated submission remains preserved until a replacement passes the full replay and scoring checks.

The best tested combination now scores 2.46 mm ADD, 2.06 mm position error, and 0.76° orientation error—an improvement in all three metrics over the frozen submission. I’m stopping the search, validating the exact saved files, and checking an extended standing hold for delayed instability.
